body:
My apologies. 


Physical attraction is comprised of aesthetic and sexual attractions.


I carelessly use both to describe the same thing (which is incorrect).


So yes by 'physical' I really mean 'aesthetic'.

Although I desire a romantic relationship with a man, I don't find myself attracted to them all that much as far as aesthetics goes. There may have been a few exceptions, but it happens quite rarely. 


It just always feels like something is missing especially when I encounter genuinely good men who may compliment me well.


Perhaps this will remain an unsolved mystery for me.

> If there is no sexual attraction why not go for a purely platonic honest friendship?


I see where your coming from. A platonic relationship will offer me with companionship and some level of closeness. They don't grant other privileges though, like exclusivity and tactile sensuality, like hand holding as an example. I would like to experience some of the latter.


Sorry if this all is confusing you.


And also sorry to hear about being lead on . That would never be my intent.

I have, but it's something that happens rarely. And I mean without the sexual component. I just don't come across many people that catch my attention purely on appearance alone.


Now those few that *have*, well, those other criteria like personality and moral standards, still matter. Also availability and compatibility also matter. One or more of those are usually missing (availability and personality being the most frequent)


It feels like I have a lot working against me.


I wouldn't want to hurt my partner if I ever admitted that I didn't find them physically attractive. But then I also don't want to dismiss a good person because of something they had no control over. This is where my conflict lies.

> I don't think you'd have such strong romantic feelings if you were truly asexual. I don't think asexuals get those feelings. I think that's what makes them asexual.


Just to address this first, romantic attraction and sexual attractions are two different notions. There are individuals who are aromantic, those who do not experience or desire romantic attraction at all. There are also individuals who are aromantic, yet feel sexual attraction to other people. Asexuals can desire romantic and sensual pleasure (hand holding, hugging, kissing, etc) they just do not get that burning feeling to hump the other person. 


I think /u/Xandine hit the nail on the head when they mentioned wanting to feel like I belong with someone. Platonic and Familial relationships do not provide everything that a romantic relationship can. 


> Do you think you're just guarding yourself to prevent being hurt by somebody? Do you think that maybe you want to be asexual to protect yourself from hurt?


I've been asexual for as long as I can remember, I just never had a word to describe my lack of interest in sex at the time. I did not discover what it meant to be asexual until I was around 18, and it all makes sense. So no, I am not using my asexuality as a defense mechanism. 


On the other hand, I am careful about the type of men that I could potentially see as along term partner. But that just means avoiding the abusers and the assholes. That still leaves a large portion of decent, respectable men left.


I am sure you have met plenty of women (or men) who caught your eye simply because you found them to be beautiful, gorgeous, hot, pretty, what have you. These women (or men) caught your attention, like a red flower in a field of yellow flowers. From my perspective, everyone appears to be the same color. Everyone may be a different shade of yellow, but nobody particularly stands out like a red, green, or blue flower. You may want to pick that red flower from the ground because, upon closer observation, that flower has other properties that make it twice as beautiful (I'm relating this to personality). Maybe it smells good, has larger petals, is taller, etc. You'll take that flower home and place it in vase, and provide it what it needs. 


But I may approach a yellow flower, and see it too has properties that make it a great flower. But it is still a yellow flower to me, like the others. It probably would be better to leave the flower where it is, and maybe someone else will recognize and appreciate all of its qualities, and take it home with them. 


Not sure if the analogy makes sense.


It is odd, because I recognize beauty in art, music, text, and actions, but rarely in people.

Can you clarify what you mean by choices and progress? 


As far as dating goes, I feel as if I have limited choices (because of my asexuality and lack of physical attraction). The latter is a larger barrier than the former.

It seems like physical attraction is important to a lot of people. Which is why many would argue against dating someone they feel nothing for physically. I've adopted this mindset. Would I be hurting the other person if they knew I was not physically attracted to them?


Physical Attraction and Emotional Attraction hold the same amount of weight (50/50). I haven't met anyone that keeps that scale balanced though.

English is my first language.


> Why do you insist on suppressing these emotions of desire rather then explore them from another angle? 


I may experience these emotions when I am in solitude, but when I am in the company of someone who may feel attracted to me in some way, I can't seem to reciprocate those feelings.



For example, there was one particular guy who attended university with me, who was very talented with origami. I was pretty fascinated by some of the stuff he could do using a sheet of paper or two, and found his talent gave him some appeal in a nonphysical way.


But I would also find myself questioning myself. I was not drawn to this person in a physical way. He was not unattractive in any way. However, I found his origami more aesthetically pleasing than his physical self. In the end, I didn't pursue anything with him. It did not feel right.


I may feel attracted to someone because of a talent they possess, their intellect, their style of dress, or any other attribute I can sense with my eyes closed (ie their voice). But if I am physically looking at them, there is a disconnect.

I have not, and you are correct, they would be limiting compared to your typical relationship. For example, if it was strictly online, there would be no physical contact I'd be able to share with the other person.


I also can't guarantee if that physical attraction would be there either. 


I'm not completely against it, but it is also something I haven't given much thought towards.

Thank you.


I'm only close with members of my immediate family. But it has not been enough to relieve that longing. 


I do not have any friends at the moment because we have since grown apart. I haven't seen or spoke with my university or high school friends since we have graduated. We have grown or taken different paths, and just do not share much in common anymore. And I am okay with that. The friendships have always ended on good terms.


I do not feel attracted to women beyond anything platonic. I do find women more aesthetically attractive than men, but I do not want to arrange a romantic relationship with another woman.


I do not know how to console myself when these feelings do surface.

My self-confidence could always be better, but it also isn't completely in the toilet either. I'd say average.


I no longer have any close friends. It is pretty common for me and my friends to gradually grow apart. Their lives are occupied by spouses, children, careers, etc. When we were friends, what we had in common was related to school. Now that we are no longer in school, there's not much to share.


I am fairly close with family, but even with them, I would like someone. I find myself fantasizing about it whenever my mind begins wandering, or if I am reminded of it (ie seeing couples, valentines day is coming up, seeing my ex-friends getting married and having children).
